Named assay getters and setters for Olink data

Source: R/npx.R
npx.Rd

Methods for getting or setting Olink-specific assays of an OlinkExperiment object. These provide convenient access to the standard Olink assay names and encourage standardization of assay names across packages.

Available methods

In the following code snippets, x is an OlinkExperiment object, value is a matrix-like object with the same dimensions as x, and ... are further arguments passed to assay (for the getter) or assay<- (for the setter).

npx(x, ...), npx(x, ...) <- value:

Get or set the matrix of Normalized Protein eXpression (NPX) values. NPX values are on a log2-like scale and are the standard quantification reported by Olink.

lod(x, ...), lod(x, ...) <- value:

Get or set the matrix of Limit Of Detection (LOD) values. A single LOD value per protein is typically broadcast across all samples.

pcount(x, ...), pcount(x, ...) <- value:

Get or set the matrix of raw protein counts. This is the raw number of detected protein molecules prior to normalization to NPX.

If i is in ..., it will be ignored and a warning will be raised. For each method described above, the name of the assay in x is always the same as the function name, e.g., npx(x) will retrieve the assay named "NPX".

See also

assay and assay<-, for the wrapped methods.

Author

Lucas

Examples

example(OlinkExperiment, echo = FALSE) # Using the class example
#> Warning: no help found for 'OlinkExperiment'

dim(npx(oe))
#> [1] 730  49
npx(oe)[1:3, 1:3]
#>           5458    5484   6711
#> IL2    -0.4439 -0.0734 0.7523
#> IL10RA -0.3931  0.4009 0.2433
#> PAPPA  -0.1184 -0.0073 0.5826

# The getter/setter wraps assay("NPX")
npx(oe) <- npx(oe) + 1

# LOD accessor
lod(oe)[1:3, 1:3]
#>           5458    5484    6711
#> IL2    -0.4181 -0.4181 -0.4181
#> IL10RA -2.4999 -2.4999 -2.4999
#> PAPPA  -2.8275 -2.8275 -2.8275
